name: Joseph Smith
role: Founder of the Latter Day Saint movement; mayor of Nauvoo and 1844 presidential candidate (1805-1844)
summary: Joseph Smith founded the Latter Day Saint movement and joined religious and civic leadership: he praised the Constitution, ran for president in 1844 on gradual compensated emancipation, prison reform, a smaller Congress, a national bank, a protective tariff and annexation of Texas and Oregon, and as a Nauvoo councilor moved ordinances giving every sect, Muslims included, equal privileges. He also taught and practised plural marriage, was received as prophet, priest and king of a planned theocratic Kingdom of God, and as mayor had the opposition Nauvoo Expositor press destroyed and declared martial law in June 1844.

property-fundamental.rationale: Defended property and sought redress for the Saints' lost Missouri lands through the Constitution, but the early law of consecration put property under church bishops, so the evidence is mixed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The 1841 ordinance he moved fined up to $500 or jailed up to six months anyone 'ridiculing, abusing, or otherwise depreciating another in consequence of his religion'.

state-harmful.rationale: Treated government as needed and divinely sanctioned: called the Constitution a heavenly banner founded in the wisdom of God and proposed reforms to government rather than its removal.

empower-police-military.rationale: Wanted the president given full power to send an army to suppress mobs and a navy to watch the coasts, while also urging cuts in the pay, number and power of government officers.

decide-locally.rationale: His platform quotes Madison on respecting the rights reserved to the states, and in 1843 he said Nauvoo stands to Illinois as the state stands to the Union; but he wanted the president able to send troops without a governor's request and told Calhoun a state refusing a federal act is in rebellion.

reviewHistory.rationale: Defended states' reserved rights and Nauvoo's chartered self-rule, but his platform also asked for federal power to suppress mobs over the head of a governor.

rehabilitation.rationale: Urged legislators to make penalties for larceny and felonies work on roads and public works where the culprit can be taught wisdom and virtue, and to turn penitentiaries into seminaries of learning; rigor and seclusion would not reform as well as reason and friendship.

traditional-family.rationale: Taught marriage as ordained of God, eternal family sealing and a husband's headship, but also introduced plural marriage, so the evidence for a conventional family is mixed.

more-religion-public.rationale: His platform calls the people to 'turn unto the Lord and live; and reform this nation', and in the Council of Fifty he described its theocracy as the people getting the voice of God and seeing it executed.

reviewHistory.rationale: His platform opens by calling the people to 'turn unto the Lord and live, and reform this nation', and he planned a Kingdom of God with a Council of Fifty.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Welcomed immigrants and gathered converts from abroad to Nauvoo; the platform welcomes people of every color, clime and tongue.

free-trade.rationale: His platform calls protecting agriculture, manufactures, navigation and commerce by a judicious tariff the highest point of government care.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The 1844 platform calls it the highest point of supervision to protect agriculture, manufactures, navigation and commerce by a judicious tariff.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Revelations he dictated give each family a stewardship of property by its needs and say 'it is not given that one man should possess that which is above another'; this was taught for the church's own order.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Explicitly urged Congress to grant a national central bank with branches in every state and territory.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The platform celebrates seventy years that 'burst the chains of oppression and monarchy' and quotes Harrison's fear that the government would end in virtual monarchy; the kingship the Council of Fifty gave him was not hereditary.

reviewHistory.rationale: Platform praises bursting the chains of oppression and monarchy and fears a virtual monarchy; he was himself later made king in the Council of Fifty, which was not hereditary.

democracy-best.rationale: Praised the elective American government and said the people are the sovereign, but also held that man cannot govern himself and favored a divine theocracy.

right-to-secede.rationale: He mocked 'nullifying Carolina' and told Calhoun that a state refusing submission to Congress is guilty of insurrection or rebellion.

political-violence-never.rationale: In 1838 he and the First Presidency backed the Danites, a private armed society formed to defend the Saints, which with him threatened retribution against any mob; the Joseph Smith Papers editors note he also said he wished to do nothing unlawful.

reviewHistory.rationale: Revelations he dictated permit war when God commands it and allow defence of one's life, and he defended armed self-defence in Missouri; he also counselled patience under repeated attack.

reviewHistory.rationale: Served at once as church president and mayor and planned a theocratic kingdom, yet quoted Madison on exempting the functions of religion from civil jurisdiction and defended religious liberty for all.

reviewHistory.rationale: Described ancient Israel's theocracy approvingly, with God making laws, and organized a Kingdom of God, yet Nauvoo ordinances and his platform rest on the Constitution.

military-superiority.rationale: Platform endorsed Washington's maxim that being prepared for war is a means of preserving peace and wanted a navy watching the coasts.

ethnic-nation.rationale: His platform welcomes neighbors from any state or country 'of whatever color, clime or tongue' and invites all the world to unite as one great family.

equal-outcomes.rationale: A revelation he dictated says it is not given that one man should possess above another, and his platform says more equality through the cities, towns and country would make less distinction among the people.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: His platform says Oregon belongs to the United States but the Union should spread west only 'when we have the red man's consent'.

restore-past-order.rationale: Platform pledges to walk the old paths of the founders and cites Harrison's aim to restore the government to its pristine health; his church claims to restore the primitive gospel.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The law of consecration he dictated gave each family a portion according to its circumstances, wants and needs, with equal claims on common stewardship property. It applied inside the church, not as state policy, and the idle were not to eat.

hereditarian-race.rationale: In 1843 he said Black people were held back by their situation: 'Change their situation with the whites, and they would be like them', pointing to educated Black men who had risen by their own minds.

national-rebirth.rationale: Platform says the republic has declined since Van Buren and calls the people to turn to the Lord and reform the nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Platform says the Union should spread from the east to the west sea, take in Texas, Mexico and Canada, and the Teachings quote him: 'We should grasp all the territory we can.'

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Preached that Judah must return and Jerusalem be rebuilt and a revelation he dictated says Judah is to flee to Jerusalem; this is stated as prophecy, not as a political right to statehood.

rule-by-example.rationale: Platform urges rendering good for evil and making honor the standard, and says reason and friendship reform better than rigor.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Built his movement on revelation and faith as a principle of action rather than reason alone.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The law of consecration he dictated provides for the poor from the bishop's storehouse but says 'he that is idle shall not eat the bread nor wear the garments of the laborer'.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: In 1843 he said that if he had anything to do with Black people he would 'confine them by strict law to their own species', while his 1844 platform says the Constitution meant what it said 'without reference to color or condition'; his words point both ways.

reviewHistory.rationale: Secondhand remarks attributed to him favor separation by law of Black and white people, while his 1844 platform says the Constitution knows no color; the record conflicts.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: In 1843 he said that if he had anything to do with Black people he would 'confine them by strict law to their own species', while his 1844 platform says the Constitution meant what it said 'without reference to color or condition'; his words point both ways.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Platform describes wicked and designing men unrobing government, corrupt legislation and politicians whose motto is 'Every man has his price'.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: His platform says a governor who becomes a mobber should be punished for murder and treason, and he told Calhoun Missouri must atone for expelling and killing Saints by the governor's order.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His platform says agriculture, manufactures, navigation and commerce 'need the fostering care of government' and asks for a national bank and a protective tariff.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Asked about Black Americans in 1843, he said he would 'confine them by strict law to their own species, and put them on a national equalization'.

reviewHistory.rationale: He is reported to have opposed Black-white marriages, fining people in two Nauvoo cases; the report is secondhand.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A revelation he dictated says beasts are ordained for man's food and raiment and that whoever forbids meat 'is not ordained of God'.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The platform says 'the people are the government, and their united voice is the only sovereign that should rule'.

population-transfer.rationale: He condemned Missouri's expulsion of 15,000 Saints 'by order of the governor, at the point of the bayonet' and called for redress.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Revelations he dictated require the church to remember the poor and needy first: surplus is consecrated to a storehouse for them, and those who do not impart their abundance are condemned.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: As mayor on 18 June 1844, fearing a mob attack, he declared Nauvoo under martial law and ordered the Legion and police to let no person or property in or out without orders.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Proposed paying members of Congress two dollars a day and board, which he said is more than the farmer gets but is honest.

head-commands-forces.rationale: His platform asks that the president be given 'full power to send an army to suppress mobs' without a governor's request.

central-bank-independence.rationale: His proposed national bank would have its directors elected yearly by the people and the people made controllers of its ways and means, not insulated from elected control.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Revelations he dictated describe the earth and all things as God's and property as a stewardship; the rich are told to impart to the poor and the poor are to be exalted as the rich are made low.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He taught that the Melchizedek priesthood 'is a perfect law of theocracy, and stands as God to give laws to the people', and that in Israel civil and ecclesiastical affairs were one.

elective-rulers.rationale: His platform says the people are the government and their united voice the only sovereign, and he would serve as president 'by the voice of a virtuous people'.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: On Zion's Camp he told men to leave rattlesnakes alone and not to kill birds or animals except to avoid hunger, and a revelation says woe to those who waste flesh needlessly.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Revelations he dictated say beasts and fowls are ordained for food and raiment, used sparingly, and warn against wasting flesh.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: A revelation he dictated says 'Wo unto you rich men, that will not give your substance to the poor' and that those who take the abundance and impart not to the poor will lift up their eyes in hell.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Revelations he dictated treat the earth as the Lord's and give members stewardships over consecrated property they hold while faithful; this was a church order.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Revelations he dictated say to be subject to the powers that be and let no man break the laws of the land; the Articles of Faith affirm obeying, honoring and sustaining the law. He did resist Missouri authorities.

religious-nation.rationale: The Council of Fifty he chaired, the planned Kingdom of God, admitted members who belonged to no church, recorded as showing that men are not consulted about their religious opinions.

religion-illusion.rationale: Presented religion as truth and revelation from God, not illusion.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Revelations he dictated set up consecration, with property deeded to the bishop and stewardships given back by need, but the arrangement was a church order rather than a plan for all of society, and his platform proposed no such reorganization.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Urged the nation to turn to the Lord and held religion central to public life.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Called for opening prisons, abolishing the cruel customs of prisons and pardoning convicts, but kept confinement or death for murder and did not address police.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: He told the Relief Society that each should act 'in the sphere allotted him or her' and not aspire to other stations, though he defended sisters laying hands on the sick.

reviewHistory.rationale: Organized the Relief Society and said the sisters were ordained in their offices, yet ordained men only to the priesthood quorums.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The revelation on marriage he dictated requires a wife to administer to her husband in plural marriage or be destroyed, and the Teachings call the husband head of the wife.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Revelations he dictated say the idler shall not eat the bread or wear the garments of the laborer, tying maintenance to work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: A revelation he dictated says that if an enemy seeks a man's life and endangers it, the enemy is delivered into his hands and he is justified.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The platform calls on the people to turn to the Lord, frustrate the designs of wicked men and make honor the standard; a revelation says when the wicked rule the people mourn.

second-chamber.rationale: His plan to shrink Congress keeps two senators per state alongside members chosen by population.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Platform opens with anxiety for all men's happiness 'both in time and in eternity', and he taught that temporal and spiritual are one.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: A revelation he dictated says to renounce war and proclaim peace and that war may be waged only after a standard of peace is lifted three times; the platform quotes Madison for amicable discussion over arms.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: In 1838 he backed the Danites, a private armed society organized to defend the Saints apart from the state militia.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Said truth should be received from wherever it comes and that he would unite men of all denominations in love, but a revelation he dictated calls his the only true and living church.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 1841 Nauvoo ordinance he moved gave Catholic, Protestant and Latter-day Saint denominations alike 'free toleration and equal Privileges'.

premarital-sex.rationale: Revelations he dictated forbid adultery and lustful looking and call for cleaving to one's wife only; sex outside marriage is not countenanced.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The Articles of Faith say the Bible is the word of God only as far as it is translated correctly; he also revised it and added further scripture.

national-church-status.rationale: As a Nauvoo councilor he moved the 1841 ordinance that Catholics, Presbyterians, Methodists, Baptists, Latter-day Saints, Quakers, Muslims and all other sects 'shall have free toleration and equal Privileges' in the city.

reviewHistory.rationale: Claimed equal rights for Presbyterians, Baptists and Catholics and defended all denominations against persecution, and the Articles of Faith allow all men to worship as they may.

simple-living.rationale: The law of the church he dictated says 'let all thy garments be plain' and forbids pride of heart.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: His platform condemns 'Democracy, Whiggery and Cliquery' for fomenting divisions to accumulate power and says it is time for a president of the United States rather than of a party.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: He told the Council of Fifty that 'in all governments or political transactions a mans religious opinions should never be called in question'.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Of an Illinois stay law he held unconstitutional he asked in 1843, 'Shall we be such fools as to be governed by its laws; which are unconstitutional? No!'

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: In 1843 he urged Nauvoo to 'go upon the hard money system altogether' with gold and silver as lawful tender, and his 1844 bank plan forbade issuing more bills than the capital in the vaults.

pay-off-national-debt.rationale: His platform calls Jackson's administration the acme of American glory because the national debt from the war 'was paid up in his golden day'.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: In 1836 he wrote approvingly of the government 'gathering the Indians, and locating them upon lands to be their own', while his 1844 platform would extend the Union to Oregon only 'when we have the red man's consent'.

no-central-bank.rationale: His platform asks Congress to grant a national bank with branches in every state and territory, its capital held by the nation and its directors elected by the people.

religious-offensive-war.rationale: A revelation he dictated says his people should not go to battle against any nation unless the Lord commands, and only after offering peace three times to an enemy that proclaimed war.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: He wrote that a newcomer from any country 'of whatever color' should be able to rejoice on setting foot on American soil.

member-state-blocks-federal-overreach.rationale: His letter to Calhoun says an act of Congress restoring citizens' rights 'is the supreme law of the land, and should a state refuse submission, that state is guilty of insurrection or rebellion'.

humans-entitled-to-use-animals.rationale: D&C 49, which he dictated, states that 'the beasts of the field and the fowls of the air ... is ordained for the use of man for food and for raiment'.

avoid-permanent-military-alliances.rationale: His platform says 'wisdom would direct no tangling alliance' and adopts Madison's aim to exclude foreign intrigues and partialities.

country-wealth-only-from-land.rationale: His platform names four main pillars of prosperity, agriculture, manufactures, navigation and commerce, not land alone.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: His platform would free the slaves and 'hire him to labor like other human beings', but a month later he proposed sending freed slaves to Texas and on to Mexico; his words point both ways.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: His platform says 'unity is power' and voices astonishment at persons and parties who 'foment discord in order to ride into power'.

political-decisions-consensus.rationale: He told the Council of Fifty that the world can be governed by 'two or three being united' and that no member should assent to anything and then find fault with it.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: He said he was ready to die defending the rights of a Presbyterian, a Baptist or any other unpopular denomination, as he had been for a Mormon.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: He married an estimated 30 to 40 plural wives from 1841, some of them already married to other men, and authorized others to practise plural marriage.

immigration-favours-shared-culture.rationale: His platform welcomes 'the neighbor from any state, or from any country, of whatever color, clime or tongue' to the soil of freedom.

conquest-no-lawful-claim.rationale: He quotes approvingly territory gained 'by fair and honorable treaty' and regions 'acquired, not by conquest, but by compact', and would take Oregon only with the Indians' consent and Texas on its own petition.

notes:
Records only what he said in the 1844 platform, his letters and sermons as compiled in the Teachings, and revelations he dictated, taken as his words. Statements on Black people and the Nauvoo Expositor rely partly on later or secondary accounts and are low confidence. His views on slavery moved from defending slaveholders' rights in the 1830s to urging compensated abolition in 1844; the latter is used.

claude-opus-5-5 later pass (2026-11-09, rules 5): brought up to rules 5 for search traffic. Replaced the Wikipedia citations with the documents they rest on, read in the Joseph Smith Papers: the 1844 Views pamphlet, the 1841 Nauvoo council minutes and ordinances he moved, the 10 June 1844 Expositor minutes, the 18 June 1844 martial-law proclamation, the Council of Fifty minutes of 11 and 18 April 1844, the January 1844 letter to Calhoun and the 1838 Documents introduction on the Danites; plus the full text of the Teachings and the revelations. Record over words now applies: the toleration ordinance answers the church-status and blasphemy statements, the Expositor and martial-law acts answer suppression and emergency powers, and his plural marriages answer monogamy. On race his words move from 1838 ('we do not believe in setting the negroes free') to 1843 (confine Black people 'by strict law to their own species', while saying their condition, not nature, held them back) to the 1844 platform (compensated emancipation by 1850; the Constitution 'without reference to color'); equality is answered as mixed. Themes searched: government (federal power, states' rights, theocracy, officials), world (expansion, alliances, war, Native Americans), economy (banking, money, tariff, consecration, debt), liberty (press, religion, prisons, martial law), society (race, marriage, women). Technology and ecology statements, and most modern policy questions, are anachronistic and stay null. Not used: the Kirtland Safety Society (no statement it settles) and D&C 134 (written by Oliver Cowdery). The Wikisource copy of the platform now refuses scripted access, so the Joseph Smith Papers copy is cited.
